inline.s: Biography of Master Shandao (Vernacular)
Biography of Master Shandao (Original Text)
the original text is excerpted from the Records of the Sages and Worthies of the Pure Land
Tang dynasty — Shandao (second patriarch of the Lotus school)
Master Shandao
his origins are unclear
During the Zhenguan reign of Emperor Taizong of Tang (627–649 CE),
he

saw the Pure Land nine-grade practice hall of Chan Master Daochuo of Xihe and said joyfully: “This truly is the essential path for entering the Buddha's stage. To practice other Dharma-gates is circuitous and arduous
difficult to accomplish; only this Pure Land Dharma-gate can swiftly transcend the cycle of birth and death.” Thereupon
with the utmost sincerity
and diligence
practicing austerely, bowing
in homage,
reciting,
and chanting day and night without cease.
Before long
Shandao
the master
arrived at the capital
Chang'an
, where he encouraged and taught
monastics and laypeople,
the fourfold assembly, to practice Buddha-recitation.
He

would, every time he entered the Buddha-recitation hall, kneel upright and recite the Buddha's name, never ceasing until his strength was spent. Coming out of the hall, he would expound and teach the Pure Land Dharma-gate to people. Practicing thus
for more than thirty years he never once lay down to sleep.

Throughout his life Master Shandao strictly upheld the precepts and dignified deportment, never transgressing in the slightest degree. Fine food and drink he would always offer to the assembly, eating only the coarse and poor himself. All the offerings and alms he received
he
used to copy the Amitābha Sutra, more than a hundred thousand scrolls in all,
and distribute them to his disciples and followers;
he painted transformation scenes of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, more than three hundred murals in all;
and he also
repaired and built stupas and monasteries, and lit bright lamps to illuminate the Buddha. Both monastics and laypeople who followed
and
received
his
teaching
were
extremely
numerous; some recited the Amitābha Sutra from a hundred thousand to five hundred thousand times, and some recited the Buddha's name ten thousand times
, or even
a hundred thousand times, each day. Among his disciples
and
followers
those who attained the Buddha-recitation samādhi were too many to record or recount.
Someone asked: “Can one attain rebirth by reciting the Buddha's name, and be born in
the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
?” Master Shandao
answered,

saying: “As you recite the Buddha's name diligently, your wish will surely be fulfilled.” Then Master Shandao recited the Buddha's name once, and at the same time a ray of light issued from his mouth; when he recited ten times or even a hundred times, the light issued forth likewise with each recitation (to prove that the merit of Buddha-recitation is true and not false)
His verse of admonition to the world said: “Gradually our skin turns to chicken-skin and our hair to crane-white, and day by day
we grow
old and frail
Look at the way we walk
— slowly it becomes the tottering gait of age
dull
and labored.
Even if you possessed countless pieces of gold and white jade
heaped to fill an entire hall, could you thereby escape the pains of decline, decay, and illness? Though you may enjoy a thousand pleasures as you please,
the death-dealing
impermanence will surely come one day
Only hasten to rely
upon
the most direct path of practice, and single-mindedly recite the name of Amitābha Buddha.”

Someone asked: “Why do you not teach people to practice visualization, but instead directly teach them to recite the name of Amitābha Buddha?” Master Shandao answered: “Beings have heavy karmic obstructions; the states to be contemplated are fine and subtle, while the mind that contemplates is extremely coarse
and restless
. Since the consciousness is agitated
and
the spirit scattered, visualization is very difficult to accomplish.
There-
fore the World-Honored One Śākyamuni, in his great compassion, took pity on beings and directly urged them to concentrate on reciting the name of Amitābha Buddha (in the original text:
“Therefore the Great Sage
(that is, Śākyamuni Buddha)
took pity and directly urged the exclusive recitation of the name”
). It is precisely because reciting the Buddha's name is easy
to accomplish
that,
continuity brings immediate birth

(at the moment of death, as long as the thought of Buddha-recitation continues without being interrupted by idle thoughts, one attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss). If one can continue this thought from moment to moment,
persisting in this practice for one's whole life
(in the original text:
“If one can continue the thought from moment to moment, for all one's life long”
), then of ten people
there will be
ten
people
reborn
, and of
a hundred people
there will be
a hundred people reborn
with not one in ten thousand failing. Why is this?
It is because
the mind does not cling outwardly to this and that in confusion, and so attains the continuity of right mindfulness
because one is in accord with Amitābha Buddha's original vow
because one does not contravene the teaching of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni
; and because
one follows the Dharma spoken by the Buddha
and
practices as taught.

[Note: The Dharma-gate of Buddha-recitation has four methods: 1. Recitation by holding the name — single-mindedly reciting the Buddha's name; 2. Recitation by contemplating the image — gazing at the Buddha's image while reciting the name with the mouth; 3. Recitation by visualization — single-mindedly visualizing the marks and adornments of the Buddha; 4. Recitation of the true mark — single-mindedly contemplating the Dharma-body, the true mark of the Buddha.

Among these four methods, which one best suits the capacities of beings — highest in merit yet easiest to practice, least in effort yet swiftest in effect? Master Shandao, who was Amitābha Buddha returned to this world, made a wise choice for us, selecting the method most suited to the capacities of beings in the Dharma-ending age — recitation by holding the name.
Master Shandao taught:
Therefore the Great Sage
(Śākyamuni Buddha)
took pity and directly urged the exclusive recitation of the name.
It is precisely because reciting the name is easy that
continuity brings immediate birth
...... I wish that all people would reflect well on this, and that whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they must
steel their hearts and restrain themselves, never neglecting it day or night

, so that when the preceding thought comes to an end, the very next thought is born in the Pure Land, forever enjoying the unconditioned joy of the Dharma, until they attain Buddhahood — is this not a joy indeed!
Once the general direction for Pure Land study and practice is settled — that one should practice exclusively the recitation of the Buddha's name (
“exclusive recitation of the name”
, because
“continuity brings immediate birth”
) — the question that immediately follows is: how should one recite the Buddha's name
so as to ensure rebirth
? Therefore, Master Shandao went on to teach:
“If one can
continue the thought from moment to moment, for all one's life long
(persisting in this practice for one's whole life)
, then of ten, ten will be born; of a hundred, a hundred will be born.
...... I wish that all people would reflect well on this, and that whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they must
steel their hearts and restrain themselves, never neglecting it day or night

, so that when the preceding thought comes to an end, the very next thought is born in the Pure Land, forever enjoying the unconditioned joy of the Dharma, until they attain Buddhahood — is this not a joy indeed!
This thoroughly and completely resolves the fundamental question of Pure Land study and practice: which method of Buddha-recitation should be adopted, and how should one recite
so as to ensure rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
? Master Shandao, Amitābha Buddha returned to this world, gave a perfect answer:
exclusively recite the name, and continuity brings immediate birth; continue the thought from moment to moment, for all one's life long,
steel your heart and restrain yourself, never neglecting it day or night
These twenty-four great characters
are the golden highway leading to the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
the guiding principle of Pure Land study and practice, the wondrous method that ensures rebirth, and the essence of Master Shandao's Pure Land teaching. One who practices thus,
“of ten, ten will be born; of a hundred, a hundred will be born”
“Conversely
if one abandons the practice of exclusive
recitation
and intermixes the practice of other Dharma-gates, then among a hundred people scarcely one or two will attain it, and among a thousand scarcely three or four will be reborn
Why is this?
Because the mind clings outwardly to this and that in confusion,
and so loses right mindfulness
because one is not in accord with Amitābha Buddha's original vow
because one contravenes the teaching of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni
because one does not follow the Dharma spoken by the Buddha and practice it accordingly
because the mind fixed on the Buddha's name cannot continue without interruption
and because inwardly one cannot single-mindedly recollect and repay the Buddha's great kindness. Although
they
also engage in practice, they are nevertheless constantly in accord with cravings for fame and profit
and such
desires, never apart from them
they delight in keeping close to confused and distracting
conditions
obstructing
themselves
and
obstructing
others in the correct practice of cultivating rebirth in the Pure Land.
“Of late

I have seen monks and laypeople from all quarters — although each differs in understanding and practice, some exclusively practicing and some practicing in a mixed way — yet as long as, from this day forward, one
concentrates single-mindedly on reciting the name of Amitābha Buddha, then of ten
there will be
ten reborn. Conversely, those who practice mixed karma
and
cannot be utterly sincere
and single-
minded
in reciting the Buddha
, even among a thousand, not one will be reborn.
“I pray that all people under heaven will carefully reflect
on the difference between these two
, and that in the course of daily life — walking, standing, sitting, and lying down — they will single-mindedly
, strictly
demand
of themselves
that they recite the Buddha's name diligently day and night without interruption, right
up until
their life
comes to an end
. Then at the moment of death, as soon as the preceding thought ceases, in the very next instant they will be born by transformation in a lotus flower in the Land of Ultimate Bliss
For endless kalpas of time to come, they will forever enjoy the pure joy of the unconditioned Dharma, until they ultimately attain Buddhahood — is this not a joy indeed!”
Master Shandao
also composed the Essay on Right Mindfulness at the Time of Death, which says: “Whoever, at the time of death, wishes to be reborn in
the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
must not fear death. And he
should
constantly reflect that this physical body of ours has very
many
kinds of suffering; it is impure
and constantly encounters all manner of evil conditions, unceasingly undergoing all kinds of vexations and entanglements

bound up and intertwined. If one can cast off this defiled and impure body and transcend to rebirth in the pure land of the West, one will personally receive boundless joy of the Dharma and be liberated from the pain of birth and death in the six
realms
through countless kalpas. This is truly a most gratifying thing, like taking off worn-out, coarse clothes and putting on wonderful,
magnificent
robes
“Therefore we should let go of this illusory body, mind, and world, and not
cling greedily to this life of pain and torment
. If we encounter illness and suffering, we should all the more reflect on the impermanence of birth and death, let go of everything
and recite the Buddha's name single-mindedly, waiting for the time of death
when Amitābha Buddha will come to receive and guide us to rebirth. We must also instruct our family and relatives, as well as those who come to visit us in illness

all who come before me should only recite the Buddha's name for me; they must not speak of idle and useless matters of the moment, nor of the rights and wrongs and family affairs at home. Neither need they comfort me with soft and loving words or wish me health and happiness, for all these are empty and showy,
utterly without benefit.
“If
the illness is critical and death is near, the family and relatives must not shed tears or weep, nor utter sounds of sighing and regret

sounds that cause sorrow, for this would confuse the mind-spirit of the dying person and make him lose the right mindfulness of reciting the Buddha and aspiring for rebirth. Simply teach the dying person to remember and recollect Amitābha Buddha and to persist in reciting the Buddha's name,
with right mindfulness
unwavering
, until his breath is exhausted. If one can meet a good spiritual friend who clearly understands the Pure Land Dharma-gate to come and constantly urge and encourage
him
to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, that is truly a great blessing.
“If one can follow
what has been said above
and apply this method, one is certain to be reborn in
the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
, of this there is no doubt.
“The matter of dying at the end of life
is of the utmost gravity
, and it is

essential to exert oneself with one's own effort. If at the moment of death one's single thought goes astray, the consequence is suffering for kalpas on end — who can take your place? Reflect well on this, reflect well on this!”
One day Master Shandao suddenly said to others: “This physical body is truly loathsome; I am about to return west to my native land of Ultimate Bliss.”
Thereupon
he climbed a willow tree in front of the monastery, and facing

west, made this vow: “May Amitābha Buddha receive and guide me, and may the Bodhisattvas protect, remember, and assist me, so that I do not lose right mindfulness and may attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.” Having said this,
he
threw himself down from the tree
and passed into rebirth
Emperor Gaozong of Tang, knowing that Master Shandao's practice was miraculous and unfathomable, therefore bestowed a plaque upon the monastery
inscribed with the name
Bright Light
Excerpted
from the Records of the Sages and Worthies of the Pure Land
Tang
— Shandao (second patriarch of the Lotus school)
Shandao — his origins are unknown
(his origins are unclear)
. During the Zhenguan era
(the Zhenguan reign of Emperor Taizong of Tang)
, he saw the Chan master Daochuo of Xihe
(Chan Master Daochuo)
at the Pure Land nine-grade practice hall and said joyfully: “This truly is the ford and the gate for entering the Buddha
(the essential path)
. To cultivate other practices is circuitous and difficult to accomplish; only this Dharma-gate swiftly transcends birth and death.”
Thereupon he practiced with utmost sincerity and austerity, bowing and reciting day and night
. Soon after
(before long)
he arrived at the capital, where he stirred and inspired the fourfold assembly
(encouraging and teaching the fourfold assembly to practice Buddha-recitation)
. Every time he entered the hall, he knelt upright and recited the Buddha's name,
never ceasing until his strength was spent
. Coming out, he would expound the Pure Land Dharma-gate.
For more than thirty years he never once slept
He upheld the precepts without the slightest transgression
. Fine food he offered to the assembly, eating only the coarse and poor himself. All the offerings
chèn
and alms
(all the offerings and alms he received)
he used to copy the Amitābha Sutra, more than a hundred thousand scrolls
, to paint three hundred walls of Pure Land transformation scenes, and to repair and build stupas and monasteries, lighting lamps to keep the light burning
(lighting bright lamps to illuminate the Buddha)
. Monastics and laypeople
(monks and laypeople)
who followed his teaching were very numerous
(whether monastics or laypeople, those who followed him and received his teaching were very many)

; some recited the Amitābha Sutra from a hundred thousand to five hundred thousand times, and some recited the Buddha's name ten thousand to a hundred thousand times a day as their daily practice. Of those among them who attained samādhi and were born in the Pure Land, there is no way to record them
(too many to record or recount)
Someone asked: “Does reciting the Buddha lead to birth in the Pure Land?” Master Shandao replied: “As you recite, so shall your wish be fulfilled
(as you recite the Buddha's name diligently, your wish to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss will surely be fulfilled)
.” Then
(thereupon)
he himself recited the name once, and a ray of light issued from his mouth; from ten times up to a hundred, the light issued likewise with each
(to prove that the merit of Buddha-recitation is true and not false)
His verse of admonition to the world says: “Gradually the skin turns to chicken-skin and the hair to crane-white; before you know it, the gait becomes tottering. Even if
(even if)
gold and jade fill the hall, can one thereby escape
(can one thereby escape)
decline, decay, and the pains of illness? Though you may enjoy a thousand pleasures, impermanence will come in the end. Only follow the direct path in practice
(only follow the most direct and convenient path in practice)
, and simply recite Amitābha Buddha.”

Someone asked: “Why do you not have people practice visualization, but directly instruct them to recite the name exclusively?” He answered: “Beings have heavy obstructions; the states are subtle while the mind is coarse, the consciousness restless and the spirit scattered
(the consciousness restless and the spirit scattered)
, so visualization is hard to accomplish. Therefore the Great Sage
(Śākyamuni Buddha)
took pity
and directly urged the exclusive recitation of the name
. It is precisely because reciting the name is easy that
continuity brings immediate birth
(at the moment of death, as long as the thought of Buddha-recitation continues without being interrupted by idle thoughts, one attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
. If one can
continue the thought from moment to moment, for all one's life long
, then of ten, ten will be born; of a hundred, a hundred will be born. Why? Because there are no external mixed conditions, and right mindfulness is attained
(the mind does not cling outwardly to this and that in confusion, and so attains the continuity of right mindfulness)
because one is in accord with the Buddha's original vow
(because one is in accord with Amitābha Buddha's original vow)
; because one does not contravene the teaching; because one follows the Buddha's words.”
“If one abandons exclusive recitation and practices mixed karma, then among a hundred scarcely one or two will attain it, and among a thousand scarcely three or four.
Why? Because mixed conditions cause confusion and agitation
(the mind clings outwardly to this and that in confusion)
, so right mindfulness is lost; because one is not in accord with the Buddha's original vow; because one contravenes the teaching; because one does not follow the Buddha's words;
because the mind fixed on the Buddha
is not
continuous
; because the mind does not
continue in recollection to repay the Buddha's kindness
(inwardly one cannot single-mindedly recollect and repay the Buddha's great kindness)

; because although one performs practices, one is constantly in accord with fame and profit; because one delights in keeping close to mixed conditions, obstructing oneself and obstructing others in the correct practice of rebirth.”
Of late
(of late)

I have seen monks and laypeople from all quarters, differing in understanding and practice, some exclusive and some mixed. But those who practice with exclusive intent — of ten, ten will be born; those who practice mixedly without sincerity, not one in a thousand.

I wish that all people would reflect well on this, and that whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they must steel their hearts and restrain themselves, never neglecting it day or night, for all their life long

. When the preceding thought ceases, the next thought is immediately born in the Pure Land; for long ages and endless kalpas they will receive the joy of the unconditioned Dharma, until they attain Buddhahood — is this not a joy indeed!”

He also composed the Essay on Right Mindfulness at the Time of Death, which says: “Whoever, at the time of death, wishes to be born in the Pure Land must not fear death. Constantly reflect that this body is full of suffering, and that impure evil conditions entangle it in every way. If one can cast off this defiled body and transcend to birth in the Pure Land, receiving boundless joy and liberation from the painful realms of birth and death, this is a most gratifying thing, like taking off worn-out clothes and changing into precious garments.

Let go of body and mind, and do not give rise to clinging. As soon as illness comes, reflect on impermanence and single-mindedly await death. You must instruct your family and those who come to inquire after you: all who come before me should recite the Buddha's name for me. They must not speak idle words of the moment or matters of family affairs. Neither need they comfort me with soft words or wish me peace and happiness, for all these are empty show without benefit. If the illness grows grave and death approaches,
the relatives must not shed tears or weep, nor utter sounds of sighing and regret, which would confuse the mind-spirit and cause the loss of right mindfulness
. Simply teach him to remember Amitābha Buddha and keep it up until his breath is exhausted.

If one can find a person who clearly understands the Pure Land to come often and encourage and urge one on, that is a very great blessing. One who applies this method will certainly be reborn, without any doubt.
The matter of death and birth is grave; one must exert one's own effort. If a single thought goes astray, one suffers for kalpas on end — who can take your place?
(if a single thought at the moment of death goes astray, the consequence is suffering for kalpas on end — who can take your place?)
Reflect on it! Reflect on it!
One day Master Shandao suddenly said to someone:
This body is loathsome; I am about to return west.
Then he climbed a willow tree in front of the monastery, and facing west he vowed:
May the Buddha receive me and the Bodhisattvas assist me,
so that I do not lose right mindfulness
and may attain birth in the Land of Peace and Nurture.
Having said this, he threw himself down and passed away. Emperor Gaozong, knowing his miraculous power, bestowed a plaque upon the monastery, inscribing it with the words
Bright Light
(Emperor Gaozong of Tang, knowing that Master Shandao's practice was miraculous and unfathomable, therefore bestowed a plaque upon the monastery
inscribed with the name
Bright Light
